concepts.label: Delete a Backup (Backup Service REST operation)
disable_safe_remove_check parameter
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - a dependency-safety guard on backup deletion, checking whether the targeted backup has dependent incremental backups before allowing removal. No existing concept covers a delete-time dependency check; closest is backup:cbbackupmgr-merge-command's own dependency logic, but that is a distinct CLI mechanism with no stated tie to this REST parameter

relations.subject: backup:delete-backup-operation
relations.evidence: The `disable_safe_remove_check` parameter is optional. It allows you to delete a backup that has incremental backups depending on it.

relations.subject: backup:safe-remove-check
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; object is a boolean literal, not a concept id, per the registry's own note that hasDefaultValue's object is frequently a literal

relations.subject: backup:delete-backup-operation
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - invalidates. When disable_safe_remove_check is set to true, the operation does not delete the dependent incremental backups - it deletes only the targeted backup - but leaves the dependents present and unusable. Neither cascadesTo (which propagates deletion) nor doesNotAffect (which is a deliberate no-op) fits an object that is left in place but broken; this predicate names that specific outcome
relations.evidence: Setting `disable_safe_remove_check` to `true` can break backup cycles and make dependent backups invalid.

relations.subject: backup:delete-backup-operation
relations.evidence: The `username` and `password` must identify an administrator with the Full Admin role.

notable_absence.finding: Like archive/create/delete-plan, this is a write operation and states its Full Admin requirement only inline in curl-syntax prose, not in a dedicated Required Permissions section - continuing the pattern flagged in backup-archive-a-repository.json.

cross_component_finding: backup:safe-remove-check's dependency logic (a backup cannot normally be deleted if incremental backups depend on it, unless a safety check is explicitly disabled) is conceptually adjacent to, but structurally distinct from, cbbackupmgr's own merge mechanism, which resolves the SAME kind of full/incremental dependency by consolidation rather than by a guarded deletion override. No page states these two are related, so they are kept as separate concepts - but both are evidence that the full-backup/incremental-backup dependency chain (backup:full-backup, backup:incremental-backup, both already promoted) is a load-bearing constraint the Backup Service enforces independently of, and by a different mechanism than, cbbackupmgr's merge command.
